testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When is drowsy driving most common?
questions.correctAnswerText: At night
questions.explanation: Drowsy driving happens most at night because people are naturally less alert when they are normally sleeping. If you must drive at night, take steps to prevent fatigue.

questions.question: What should you do when making a tight turn?

options.text: Do not use your mirrors because they distract you
Use your mirrors, but not very often

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors often
questions.explanation: You must always know what is around you. Check your mirrors often. This is especially important when merging, changing lanes, turning, or making tight turns.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal after starting the engine?
questions.correctAnswerText: A few seconds
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal within a few seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: What happens when there is more alcohol in the body?

options.text: The liver will digest it faster
The alcohol will have less effect
It takes longer for the body to remove it

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes longer for the body to remove it
questions.explanation: The body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more alcohol consumed, the longer it takes the body to remove it.

questions.question: What should you do when it is hard to see other vehicles at dawn or dusk?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your lights on
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in bad weather, use your headlights on low beam to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: What will a CDL applicant be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.correctAnswerText: Check the engine oil level
questions.explanation: The vehicle inspection test includes checking the oil level. You must show that it is safe to operate.

questions.question: What happens if spring brakes are used while hauling a heavy load?

options.text: A complete stop takes a long time
A complete stop takes a short time

questions.correctAnswerText: A complete stop takes a long time
questions.explanation: Spring brakes do not work on all axles. If spring brakes activate due to low air pressure, your vehicle will need more distance to stop, especially with a heavy load.

questions.question: Where is the tire load rating shown?

options.text: On the side of the tire
On the inside of the tire
On the inside of the driver's door

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side of the tire
questions.explanation: The tire load rating shows the maximum safe weight a tire can carry. This information is printed on the side of the tire.

questions.question: Is it good to look far ahead while driving?

options.text: No, because you cannot do anything about hazards far ahead
Yes, to spot hazards as early as possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, to spot hazards as early as possible
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards early and respond safely.

questions.question: How should you look at a mirror while driving?

options.text: Use only the driver's side mirror

questions.correctAnswerText: Look quickly
questions.explanation: Look at mirrors briefly. If you look too long, you travel a long distance without seeing the road ahead.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation in your personal car, what must you do?

options.text: Your CDL will not be affected.
Law enforcement will tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must notify your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction, no matter what vehicle you were driving. This rule does not apply to parking violations.

questions.question: When do you first feel the effects of alcohol?

options.text: Only after several drinks have been consumed.

questions.correctAnswerText: With the first drink.
questions.explanation: Alcohol starts to affect you with the first drink. Driving while impaired by alcohol is both illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What does an alcohol evaporator do in an air brake system?

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator adds alcohol to the air brake system. This helps prevent ice from building up inside the system.

questions.question: What does rust around wheel nuts usually mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts usually means the nuts are loose. Check how tight the wheel nuts are before you start driving.

questions.question: When does antifreeze help keep an engine working properly?

options.text: But only if it is cold outside.
Both when it is cold and hot outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both when it is cold and hot outside.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Antifreeze is important all year, not just in cold weather.

questions.question: Are rims with welding repairs safe to use?

options.text: Are not safe to be used.
Are acceptable only when traveling at speeds under 40 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not safe to be used.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded are never safe to use.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap during a pre-trip inspection, what should you check?

options.text: Make sure there is a gap between the kingpin and the locking jaws.
Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking jaws are loose.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: Look into the fifth wheel gap and check that the locking jaws are completely closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: While driving, what holds spring brakes in place?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure
questions.explanation: While driving, air pressure holds spring brakes in place. If the air pressure drops too low, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, what should you do?

options.text: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
Pull in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will help you regain control.

questions.question: When checking windshield wiper blades, how should they be?
questions.correctAnswerText: Secure.
questions.explanation: Check your wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and proper attachment to make sure they are secure.

questions.question: What should a driver do?

options.text: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
Only use turn signals if another vehicle is next to you.
Do not use a turn signal if the lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: When shifting gears, do NOT base your decision on:

options.text: What the vehicle next to you is doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: What the vehicle next to you is doing.
questions.explanation: Shift gears based on your engine's rpm range or your speedometer. Do not shift based on other vehicles around you.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you press the brake pedal?

options.text: Push down quickly with both feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push down gradually.
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down gradually. This helps your vehicle stop smoothly and safely.

questions.question: Shortly after changing a tire, you should:

options.text: Stop to check that the lug nuts are still tight.
Let air out of the tire to 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to check that the lug nuts are still tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short time later and recheck that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: On a long downhill slope, how should you brake?

options.text: Use the brakes mostly and downshift sometimes.
Downshift first, then use the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift first, then use the brakes.
questions.explanation: On a long downhill slope, downshift to a lower gear first. Then use the brakes. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. The engine's braking power in a lower gear helps control your speed.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, how is the parking brake applied?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull a yellow diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, pull the yellow diamond-shaped knob outward to apply the parking brake. Push it inward to release it.

questions.question: What should happen before air pressure drops below 55 psi in an air brake system?

options.text: The warning light should turn on.
The vehicle will be unable to shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The warning light should turn on.
questions.explanation: The warning light must turn on before the air pressure drops below 55 psi. If it does not, the vehicle is not safe to drive.

questions.question: As a truck driver with a load, you are responsible for everything EXCEPT:

options.text: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Knowing the phone numbers of all fire departments on your route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect your cargo, check for overloading or poor weight balance, and ensure cargo is properly secured. You do not need to know every fire department's phone number.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must complete a full inspection. You must explain to the examiner what you are checking and why.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire missing one or two lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Always check that your tires and rims are in good condition before driving.

questions.question: Driving at night is usually:

options.text: More difficult than driving during the day.
Easier than driving during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Night driving is harder than day driving. You cannot see hazards as well. Headlight glare can hurt your vision. There are also more tired drivers on the road at night.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires from different makers
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that your tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch of tread. Do not use tires of different sizes.

questions.question: When parked on a flat surface, you should:

options.text: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from rolling.
Use wheel chocks only after you apply the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to stop your vehicle from rolling.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. This is especially important if your vehicle does not have spring brakes. Wheel chocks prevent the trailer from rolling.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop a short distance later to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.
Add air to the new tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you change a tire, stop a short distance down the road. Then check that all the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When placing warning triangles on the road, you should:

options.text: Hold the triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
Keep the triangles hidden behind your back until you place them.
Hold the triangles as low as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the triangles between yourself and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: For your safety, carry the warning triangles between your body and the oncoming traffic when you place them.

questions.question: When slowing down, you should ____ to warn other drivers.
questions.correctAnswerText: Tap your brakes lightly
questions.explanation: Before you slow down, tap your brakes lightly. This makes your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Is not available on most trucks.
Does not help in most situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on newer trucks.
questions.explanation: Starting between 1997 and 1999, ABS became required on most commercial vehicles, trailers, and dollies.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, slow down. This gives you more time to see and react to hazards.

questions.question: When driving, it is important to:

options.text: Avoid using your mirrors in heavy traffic.
Look only ahead and to the right.
Look ahead, to the sides, and in your mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead, to the sides, and in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: You must know what is happening all around your vehicle at all times. Look ahead and check your mirrors regularly on both sides.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer, you should:

options.text: Cover the trailer with a heavy blanket.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the trailer doors closed.
questions.explanation: Do not open the trailer doors if there is a cargo fire, especially if the cargo includes hazardous materials. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes the fire worse.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator is most important:
questions.correctAnswerText: In cold weather.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to prevent ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system loses pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: In a dual air brake system, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully if one air system loses pressure. If air pressure gets too low while driving, you should stop and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: After you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off after a few seconds.
Stay on until you turn them off manually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off after a few seconds.
questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off after a few seconds. If they stay on, something may be wrong with the vehicle.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
The water has nowhere to drain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fresh rain mixes with oil on the road.
questions.explanation: Roads are very slippery when rain first starts. The water mixes with oil drippings that have not washed away yet, creating a dangerous, slippery surface.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, belts should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for tightness.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, check all belts for tightness and wear. Learn how much give is correct for each belt.

questions.question: If one-fourth of the leaves are missing from a leaf spring during inspection:

options.text: The driver can drive at reduced speeds.
The vehicle must be taken out of service until fixed.
The vehicle is fine to drive since most of the spring is still there.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle must be taken out of service until fixed.
questions.explanation: Check leaf springs for broken or missing leaves. If one-fourth or more leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service.

questions.question: On a vehicle with power steering, the hoses should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: When inspecting power steering, check the hoses, pumps, and fluid levels. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: When inspecting the fifth wheel gap, you should check that:

options.text: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: The locking jaws are fully closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a trailer coupling, make sure the fifth wheel locking jaws are closed tightly around the kingpin shank, not the kingpin head.

questions.question: Multi-speed axles and auxiliary transmissions are used to:

options.text: Make a vehicle operate more smoothly

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide extra gears
questions.explanation: Many vehicles use multi-speed rear axles and auxiliary transmissions to provide extra gears.

questions.question: If you feel tired and yawn a lot while driving, you should:

options.text: Pull over and take a nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and take a nap.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired while driving, stop and sleep. Do not try to reach your destination while tired—it is dangerous. Caffeine alone will not keep you safe.
